free_tier.stated: free trial: USD 10 one-time credit, 1 sandbox at a time, up to 2 vCPU and 1 GiB RAM, up to 32 GiB root disk, 100 services per org and 20 per sandbox; ephemeral with 1-hour sessions. Cloud access is by request (private beta) at USD 0 per trial. Builder is USD 20 a month with USD 20 of usage included

per_object_cap.notes: a sandbox has a disk ceiling rather than an object cap; the card does not carry it

retention.notes: Disk durability across instance stops and deletions is not documented.

egress.terms: no egress allowance or price is published on the pricing page; the docs describe outbound network rules that can be restricted to allowed hosts. Persistent volumes are USD 0.15 per GiB-month and snapshots USD 0.08 per GiB-month

interface_detail: CLI (msb), SDKs for Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go and Ruby, and REST endpoints over HTTPS at api.microsandbox.dev with an MSB_API_KEY bearer token; an MCP server card is published

limits.value: USD 10 one-time trial credit; 1 sandbox at a time, up to 2 vCPU and 1 GiB RAM; ephemeral 1-hour sessions
up to 32 GiB root disk per sandbox; 100 services per org and 20 per sandbox; 1 sandbox at a time on the free trial

limits_note: Session cap, idle-reap and network policy are not documented.

identity_cost.detail: a name, an email and a password are required at signup; no card or phone number appears on the signup page. Cloud access is by request through a waitlist that asks for an email

reliability_note: no reliability event recorded in the source passes
confidence_note: the pricing page was read on 2026-10-22 and states the free pool in computer-hours with a hard cap and no overage. The pool is what makes the duty cycle computable: 5 vCPU-hours a month is about 10 minutes a day

evidence.proved: listed in the peli-cloud corpus card at commit f6a71ab0; the card is the source, not the vendor page
egress is open by default and no allowance or price is stated
evidence.quote: by default, sandboxes can reach the public internet.

evidence.proved: the page states the session clock and idle reap recorded here, or states that it publishes none
evidence.quote: SSH inactivity timeout keeps its 10-minute default, but you can now change it.

evidence.proved: the free offer is a USD 10 one-time trial credit, not a monthly compute pool
the free allowance is denominated in USD credit, not compute hours
the free allowance is a one-time credit with no stated metering basis
the free trial caps sessions at one hour and runs one sandbox at a time
the free trial root disk ceiling is 32 GiB, not 8 GiB
the signup page asks for an email address
the signup form requires a password of 8 to 128 characters
the pricing page prices persistent volumes but publishes no egress line
the managed cloud exposes a documented API reference and a dashboard
the managed cloud is driven through a documented REST API and CLI
evidence.quote: See [context commands](https://docs.microsandbox.dev/cli/management.md#msb-context) for JSON output and troubleshooting.

evidence.proved: paid tiers convert their monthly fee to usage credit and unused credit does not roll over
evidence.quote: your monthly payment becomes usage credit. extra usage is billed at the rates below. monthly credit does not roll over.

extras.keep_rate_basis: billed for uptime (no suspension feature published)

shape.note: the free shape: 1 vCPU, 512 MiB and 8 GiB of disk, three at a time

session_cap.note: no sandbox session clock; a separate SSH inactivity timeout defaults to 10 minutes and is independent of sandbox idle

extras.price_note: a price without a shape and a horizon is not a price; both columns are kept because the two seed models disagree and neither is wrong
extras.free_tier_kind_basis: decided from the page read on 2026-10-22

ps.price: a 1 GiB durable-storage cap on the free pool
